basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 19-21.' and it opens 'Vers. 19-21. Nomen uni Ada, et nomen alteri Sella. Genuitque Ada Jubal. Ipse fuit pater'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 19-21. Nomen uni Ada, et nomen alteri Sella. Genuitque Ada Jubal. Ipse fuit pater canentium cum cithara et organo. De hoc Josephus dicit: « Jubal musicam amavit, psalterium et citharam laudavit. Et ne unquam ab humana memoria elaberentur ea quae invenerat, in duabus columnis, una lateritia, | altera lapidea, descripsit, cum Adam praedicare audisset duo diluvia et omnium exterminationem. »
